payload.body:
Task 1 (hand evaluator) approach: pure ES module site/wwyhd-eval.js, no deps, no clock, no randomness.

Score encoding: categoryIndex * 15^5 + the five ranking ranks in base 15 (ranks 2..14, zero-padded to five slots). Category index 0..8 maps to the nine names in M4 order, so handCategory(score) is Math.floor(score / 15^5) into that table. Max score ~6.9M, comfortably an integer.

Seven-card best-five: enumerate all C(n,5) subsets (21 at most for 7 cards) and take the max five-card score. Chosen over a clever 7-card ranker because Charlie has to be able to read it; 21 subsets costs nothing.

Wheel handled by scoring A2345 as ranks [5,4,3,2,1] (ace low), so it sits below 6-high and Broadway [14,13,12,11,10] sits on top, which is what M3 asks for.

Validation (M5): array of 5..7 two-char cards, rank in 23456789TJQKA, suit in shdc, no duplicates; anything else throws.

Approach: a nine-hand ladder, one concrete seven-card hand per category in the M1 order (high card, pair, two pair, three of a kind, straight, flush, full house, four of a kind, straight flush), each chosen so its best five is unambiguously that category and nothing better (suit counts checked by hand so no hand is an accidental flush; no accidental straights). Legs (a)-(h) are the eight adjacent comparisons on that ladder; leg (l) reuses the same nine hands for handCategory and asserts the returned set is exactly the nine strings.

Where the Proof spells hands out verbatim (legs (i), (j), (k), (m)) the exam uses those literal arrays unchanged. The pair rung of the ladder is deliberately M2's own seven-card hand so the ladder and legs (i)/(k) agree on one hand.

Score encoding is the implementer's choice, so nothing asserts a numeric score value: the pins are ordering (>), equality (toBe between two evaluate calls), Number.isInteger, and toThrow. Import is `// @ts-ignore` over `from "../site/wwyhd-eval.js"`, as tools/portrait-dither.test.ts does. Expected red at BASE for one reason: site/wwyhd-eval.js does not exist yet.

payload.body:
Examiner: exam handed in at tools/wwyhd-eval.test.ts (21 tests, 58 expect() calls). No EXAM PATHS line for this task, so it sits where the Proof names it. Nothing else in the tree is touched; site/wwyhd-eval.js is left for the implementer.

Red at BASE for exactly one reason: `error: Cannot find module '../site/wwyhd-eval.js'` — the implementation does not exist yet. No other failure mode.

Leg-to-test map (every leg has at least one assertion):
- (a)-(h) [M1] -> one test each in 'M1: the category ladder', eight adjacent comparisons up a nine-rung ladder of concrete seven-card hands, plus a ninth test reading the whole ladder end to end (catches a non-adjacent collision that every adjacent step still passes) and asserting Number.isInteger on all nine (M1's integer clause on seven cards).
- (i) [M2] -> M2's two hands verbatim, K-kicker > Q-kicker.
- (j) [M3] -> three tests: the two wheels equal (suit-independence), both below the six-high straight (the wheel is the LOWEST straight), broadway above all three. Hands verbatim.
- (k) [M1] -> five-/six-/seven-card A A K 9 7 all Number.isInteger and all toBe equal; K K Q 7 2 below all three. Hands verbatim.
- (l) [M4] -> per-rung name check (the hand rides in the expected object so a failure names the hand), plus a sorted-set check that the nine names are exactly the nine strings.
- (m) [M5] -> four tests, each pairing the throw with leg (m)'s corrected hand returning an integer. The pairing is load-bearing: an evaluate() that threw on everything would pass the throw half alone.

Readings a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct:
1. No numeric score is asserted anywhere. Task 1 Context makes the encoding the implementer's choice, so the exam pins only ordering, equality between two evaluate() calls, Number.isInteger, and toThrow. Any correct evaluator passes regardless of its base or category offsets.
2. M5 pins no exception message, so the exam uses a bare toThrow(). The implementer is free to word the four errors as they like.
3. The nine ladder hands were each hand-checked for accidental categories (suit counts across all seven, and runs across all seven, not just the intended five). A hand that quietly made a better category than its name would turn a real failure green; the file says so in a header note so nobody 'tidies' one.
4. The pair rung of the ladder is deliberately M2's own seven-card hand, so the ladder, leg (i) and leg (k) all agree on one hand.

Mutation-checked before handing in, against a throwaway reference implementation in gitignored scratch (deleted; never written to site/). Nine deliberate defects, all caught: wheel scored ace-high (2 fail), duplicate check removed (1), length bounds removed (2), notation check removed (1), straight/flush swapped (3), pair kickers dropped (1), suit folded into the score (5), 'three of a kind' renamed 'trips' (2), best-five search replaced by the first five cards (1). The correct reference passes 21/21.

No unsatisfiable legs.

Done at c3b4a05. Footprint is exactly the task's FILES: site/wwyhd-eval.js (237 lines) and tools/wwyhd-eval.test.ts (147). All four proof commands green, suite 1020 pass / 0 fail (991 at BASE, so 29 new).

Decisions a later session would otherwise have to rediscover:

1. Score encoding is category * 15^5 + five ranking ranks in base 15. Base 15 (not 13 or 14) because the ace is 14 and each slot needs its own digit with no carry into the slot above; that carry-free property is what guarantees M1 and M2 together. Max score is under 7M, so scores are safe integers and plain > compares them. handCategory() is Math.floor(score / 15^5) into the CATEGORIES array, which is why that array must never be reordered.
2. The wheel scores as ranks [5,4,3,2,1]. The ace comes out as 1, below the deuce, because in A2345 the ace is the low end of the run. That is what puts the wheel below every other straight without a special case anywhere else.
3. Best-five is brute force over all C(n,5) subsets, 21 at most. Deliberate: a 7-card ranker would be faster and unreadable, and this runs once per page view.
4. evaluate() throws (RangeError) rather than coping on a short/long/duplicate/malformed hand. A duplicate means the deck itself is broken, so a hand file with one must halt the check tool rather than score.
5. handCategory() also throws on a score outside the nine categories, on the theory that an out-of-range score means a caller did arithmetic on a score and a clamped answer would put a confident wrong hand name on the reveal page.

Verification beyond the exam legs: cross-checked against a separately written reference categoriser over 40,000 dealt hands of sizes 5, 6 and 7 (deterministic LCG deal), zero category mismatches and zero pairwise ordering mismatches, plus spot checks for royal-flush ties across suits, steel wheel over quad aces, two-pair kicker, ace-high over king-high flush, nines full over eights full, paired-board straight ties, board-plays flush, full house from two trips, and six suited cards. The scratch script was deleted before the commit and is not in the tree.

No state exam in this task's Proof, so state.reached is left unset.
